newsitem.title: USA: Centennial Technologies faces new lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Centennial Technologies faces new lawsuit.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc., whose fired chief executive faces charges of insider trading, was slapped with yet another class action lawsuit by investors who bought the personal computer memory card maker's stock, a law firm said Friday.

The suit, filed in U.S. District Court in Boston by the New York law firm of Zwerling, Schacter & Zwerling, accused Centennial of violating securities laws in allegedly reporting "materially overstated" financial results between Aug. 21 and Feb. 10.

The complaint also alleged that Centennial's former Chairman and Chief Executive Emanuel Pinez, "improperly accounted for sales and inventory and engaged in insider trading," the firm said in a statement.

Pinez, who founded Centennial, was dismissed as chief executive in February and subsequently charged by the Securities and Exchange Commission and the U.S. Attorney's office with insider trading and falsifying sales figures.
Pinez was denied bail and has been held in a Plymouth, Mass., jail. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The Billerica, Mass.-based company then it would restate its earnings to show a loss for the past 3-1/2 years rather than a profit. Centennial, which faces at least six other similar lawsuits, was delisted from the New York Stock Exchange as of Feb. 29.
